q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of cakes per kg?
title: Cake carbon footprint per kg
short: Weigh each ingredient per kg of cake, such as flour, sugar, eggs, oil, butter and cocoa, and use supplier or published figures. Add oven fuel or electricity, mixing, chilling and packing, then divide the bakery's energy by kg of cake passed.

ul: Flour, sugar and oil or butter by weight.
Eggs, milk and cream, often the largest per-kg ingredients.
Ovens on PNG, LPG, diesel or electricity.
Cold storage, trays, boxes and wrappers.

p: Report per kg by recipe; cream and butter-rich cakes differ clearly from plain sponges.

example.title: Worked example: cake bakery per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 23,140 / 40,000 = 0.579 kg CO2 per kg
Add ingredients and packaging for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
